title: Wrap a failed read in an exception that names the file

blocks.text: A handler should be able to react to *which* file failed without parsing the message. Write the checked `FileProcessingException` and a `FileProcessor` that uses it.

items: `FileProcessingException(String message, String fileName, Throwable cause)` and `getFileName()`.

`FileProcessor(FileStore store)` and `int countLines(String fileName)`: read the file through `store.read(fileName)` and return how many lines it has (`String.lines()` counts them). When the store throws an `IOException`, throw `FileProcessingException` with the message `Error processing file: <fileName>` and that file name.

blocks.text: The exception may be caught, logged and rethrown by several layers: think about what the original failure should look like to the last of them, and whether any of them should be able to change the exception's data.

cases.says: A file the store can read has its lines counted.
A failed read becomes a FileProcessingException whose message and getFileName() name the file.
The IOException itself is the cause, so its message and stack trace are not lost.
Every context field of the exception is final, so no layer can change what another reads.

concepts: The (message, cause) constructor lets a catch block keep the original failure as the cause.
Extra context lives in final fields with getters, so a handler never parses the message.
